arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.

stkh_req__ai_platform__agent_execution.content: The SW-platform shall execute AI-based agents with defined scheduling and resource budgets per criticality domain.
stkh_req__ai_platform__agent_execution.rationale: AI-based agents share compute resources with vehicle functions of higher criticality and therefore need bounded and predictable resource usage.
stkh_req__ai_platform__agent_execution.title: Deterministic AI Agent Execution

feat_req__ai_platform__agent_execution.content: The platform shall schedule AI workloads via the existing execution management mechanisms with configurable resource budgets per criticality domain.
feat_req__ai_platform__agent_execution.title: AI Agent Resource Budgets

comp_req__feo__act_alloc_error.content:
During initialization (i.e. in the startup function of an activity), activities shall check for resource allocation
and report an error to the executor in case of failure.
comp_req__feo__act_alloc_error.title: Activity resource allocation error

aou_req__communication__1.content:
It shall be ensured that enough memory is configured for shared memory instances,
in order that LoLa can perform all necessary allocations (e.g. push-back on a Vector).
aou_req__communication__1.title: Monotonic Semi-Dynamic Memory Allocation

aou_req__os__nonroot.content:
No process running on the SW-platform shall request root privileges.

Note: The root privilege is dangerous for security and safety as it destroys process isolation.
aou_req__os__nonroot.title: No Root Privileges

aou_req__feo__on_target_crates.content:
Only the following crates of the FEO module shall be used to build code that runs on
targets in release builds.

- feo
- feo-cpp-build
- feo-cpp-macros
- feo-time
aou_req__feo__on_target_crates.title: on_target_crates

mod_view_sta__os__os.content:
The module "OS" is not a part of the S-CORE SW-Platform, but it is a crucial external SW element.
Its components are modelled in S-CORE to be able to describe dependencies of S-CORE features to this external component.
As it is external to S-CORE, the (folder/file) structure of the documentation may be different from the other modules.
Its main content is the operating system environment (sometimes also already called a "SW platform").
But also other SW components are modelled as a part of it as these are often provided by the "OS" supplier.
One example of these "other" SW components are the C/C++ libs which may come from a processor manufacturer instead.
S-CORE expects to support integration of more than one operating system, so these may be seen already in this module view,
as different components. Requirements on this OS integration are documented in :need:`doc__os_requirements`.

   :align: center
